2. `git branch --merged origin/main` — confirms the feature branch's tip is an ancestor of the integration branch (a squash or rebase merge will *not* show here; use `git log origin/main --oneline --grep=<PR#>` or `git cherry origin/main <branch>` instead).
3. `git log <branch> --not origin/<branch>` — commits on the local branch never pushed; must be empty before deleting.

Deleting is safe only when 2 shows the content landed and 3 is empty. Unverified: whether "merged" here means merged locally, merged on the remote's default branch, or a merged PR — those give different answers to both questions.
